# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 98 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_098_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 98

**1** Jesus said: "The kingdom of the Father is like a man who wished to kill a powerful man.

**2** In his own house, he drew his sword and stuck it into the wall in order to find out whether his hand could carry through.

**3** Then he slew the powerful man."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** The Parable of the Assassin is unique to Thomas and is one of the most provocative parables in the Jesus tradition. Structure: preparation (private rehearsal) leads to determination tested leads to execution. The point is: the kingdom requires tested, prepared, decisive commitment.

**"The powerful man"** — *rome nkhom*: the adversary who must be overcome. In the context of Thomas, this may be the world, the ego, or the forces of darkness.

**"Whether his hand could carry through"** — not just physical strength but will and follow-through. The test is of resolve.

**"Wished," "stuck," and "slew"** — SOPHIA follows EMET's more literal rendering. The older diction preserves the deliberateness. All three agents agree substantially.

**Theological Note:** The parable is not an endorsement of violence — it is a parable of preparation and commitment to the kingdom. The comparison is structural, not moral. No Synoptic parallel exists.
